framing.aom: DISAMB-adjacent controlled contextual variation, not a clean homonym-style DISAMB task.
framing.mom: Candidate intervention family for testing whether contextual preference shifts are recovered in residual states or sparse feature bases.
framing.vagueness: Direct bridge to Sorites-sensitive vague predicates: pile and heap have graded boundaries, while stack depends on ordered arrangement and material affordance.

methodological_caveats: Do not report as simple truth-conditional accuracy; many labels are preference targets.
Use log-probability margins over candidate labels: log P(expected) - max log P(other candidates).
Interpret borderline items as graded transitions, especially pile-to-heap with increasing amount.
The candidate set excludes mound; ordered sand items should therefore be interpreted as pile-vs-heap-vs-stack only.
Prompts avoid direct target leakage: no pile, heap, stack, heaped, stacked, or mound in item text.
predictions: Ordered wood and ordered boxes should increase the stack margin.
Sand should suppress the stack margin even when spatially regular.
Large disordered quantities should increase the heap margin.
Quantity should induce a gradual pile-to-heap shift rather than a sharp boundary.
